summary: Tested billing refactor (billing_date -> plan_expiry_date). 8/10 backend tests pass, 2 fail due to CRITICAL BUG: generate_first_invoice=true silently fails because CronJobService._create_first_invoice() references a non-existent method self._get_next_invoice_number(). All subscriber-expiry-date math, migration endpoint, sample CSV, and admin cron window all work correctly. Frontend UI elements (Plan Start Date field, auto expiry display, 'Generate First Invoice Now?' toggle, Migrate to Expiry Billing button, Bulk Upload dialog with plan_start_date_N columns) render correctly.

critical.issue: First invoice is NOT created. Subscriber is created successfully but invoice generation silently fails. Backend log shows: "First invoice creation failed for <sub_id>: 'CronJobService' object has no attribute '_get_next_invoice_number'". The exception is swallowed by try/except in routers/operator.py:1283-1284 so API returns 200 but no invoice row exists.

Calls self._get_next_invoice_number(operator['id'], prefix) which is undefined on CronJobService. Should use the same pattern used at line 483 of the same file: `from utils import generate_invoice_number_atomic; invoice_number = await generate_invoice_number_atomic(self.db)`.
Cannot end-to-end verify the mark-paid expiry extension because the prerequisite first invoice is never created (blocked by bug above). Once fixed, re-run test_mark_paid_extends_expiry_by_validity.

minor.issue: For a subscriber with plan_expiry_date=today+2d (within default 3-day notice window), the cron endpoint returned 200 but did NOT create an upcoming invoice. test_cron_creates_invoice_when_in_notice_window was skipped (result was 0 invoices). Could indicate the notice-window branch in cron_service.generate_upcoming_invoices still isn't matching plan_expiry_date correctly, or the subscriber needed an existing invoice history to qualify. Needs deeper investigation.

integration_issues.flow: Create Subscriber with Generate First Invoice toggle ON
integration_issues.issue: End-user will toggle 'Generate First Invoice Now?' ON, click Create Subscriber, see success toast, but NO invoice will appear in Invoices list. Caused by the backend AttributeError bug above.

issues: Plan Start Date uses the browser's native date picker (<input type='date'>) instead of the shadcn Calendar component used elsewhere. Minor inconsistency with app design system.

action_items: FIX services/cron_service.py:699: replace `await self._get_next_invoice_number(operator['id'], prefix)` with the existing helper `from utils import generate_invoice_number_atomic; invoice_num = await generate_invoice_number_atomic(self.db)` (same as line 483). This is a one-line fix.
After fix, re-run test_billing_expiry_refactor.py; tests test_generate_first_invoice_true_creates_invoice and test_mark_paid_extends_expiry_by_validity should pass.

Investigate why cron generate_upcoming_invoices does not create an upcoming invoice for a subscriber whose plan_expiry_date is within the notice window (auto_invoice_days_before=3). Verify the query in services/cron_service.generate_upcoming_invoices uses `plans.plan_expiry_date <= today+notice` correctly.
Consider removing the silent try/except in routers/operator.py:1283-1284 or at least logging at ERROR level + returning a warning in the API response so such failures are visible to UI.
Optional: switch Plan Start Date input to shadcn Calendar component for design consistency.
critical_code_review_comments: routers/operator.py:1283-1284: broad try/except around first-invoice creation swallows real errors as WARNING. This is how the AttributeError got masked. At minimum log at ERROR, ideally surface to client.
services/cron_service.py:_create_first_invoice uses a non-existent helper method. This function was never end-to-end tested after the refactor — add an integration test.
The mark-paid expiry-extension logic in routers/operator.py:1901-1940 correctly implements base_date = max(old_expiry, paid_date). Good.
migrate-to-expiry-dates endpoint at routers/operator.py:1368 is idempotent (skips plans with existing plan_expiry_date). Good.

success_rate.frontend: 90% (UI renders correctly; integration fails because of backend bug)

context_for_next_testing_agent: Re-run /app/backend/tests/test_billing_expiry_refactor.py after cron_service.py:699 fix. Export REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL before pytest (`export REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL=$(grep REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL /app/frontend/.env | cut -d= -f2)`). The 3 cron tests and 2 first-invoice tests are the ones to watch. Also verify test_cron_creates_invoice_when_in_notice_window no longer skips.
rca of the issue: ROOT CAUSE: During the billing refactor, the new _create_first_invoice method was added to services/cron_service.py but it calls self._get_next_invoice_number(operator_id, prefix) — a method that does not exist on CronJobService. The correct pattern used elsewhere in the same file (line 483) is `from utils import generate_invoice_number_atomic; invoice_number = await generate_invoice_number_atomic(self.db)`. REPRODUCTION: POST /api/operator/subscribers with {generate_first_invoice:true, plans:[{plan_id:<any monthly plan>}], ...}. Response is 200. Check backend logs — you'll see 'First invoice creation failed ... object has no attribute _get_next_invoice_number'. GET /api/operator/invoices?subscriber_id=<new id> returns []. MITIGATION: One-line fix in cron_service.py:699 to use the existing atomic helper. Remove or replace the silent `except Exception as inv_err: logger.warning(...)` in routers/operator.py:1283 so similar bugs aren't masked.
